comparisons.name: CrossProfile

qwen_primary_budget.condition: Qwen2.5-7B at primary 0.6 memory budget, averaged over ownership variants

other_findings: Rarest-first and relevance-first policies depend on whether support or decoy facts are private; neither is robust across ownership configurations.
In the classic hidden-profile configuration, the paper reports a 23–31 percentage-point gap between relevance filtering and rarest-first selection.
Masking or shuffling source-attribution tags raises accuracy by 13–24 percentage points in the classic configuration, with fact order held fixed.
In natural discussions, the complete transcript can perform worse than no notes, indicating information loss can occur before the memory-selection stage.

cross_benchmark_rules: Do not compare accuracy across different task or outcome definitions.
Report the paper's original configuration and a matched local configuration separately.
Pin model/provider/revision, prompt, agent count, communication rounds, tools, seeds, tokenizer, tokens, compute and evaluator.
Include single-agent/private and full-information upper-bound controls where the task supports them.
Include unstructured, round-robin, broadcast, structured elicitation and adaptive inquiry baselines under matched budgets.
Report both process and outcome metrics; correct decisions by luck do not prove good information acquisition.
Report the worst ownership, language, evidence-quality and rights condition alongside averages.
Use held-out templates/domains and confidence intervals before superiority claims.
A public paper, model card, or code license is not blanket permission for third-party data or real participant conversations.
claim_ceiling: metadata comparison only; no external payload downloaded, no external benchmark reproduced, and no superiority claim established
